analysis:
The only change in StandaloneServer.swift (head lines ~1538-1564) is in ensureMemoryHeadroomForLoad. Before evicting an idle cached model, the loop now makes one attempt to reclaim memory without eviction. It calls a new releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad(), which awaits GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments() and then, if nativeMiMoReclaimAllowed, calls MLX.Memory.clearCache(). The initial poolDropped flag is !GlobalKVCacheBudget.busyEnginesKeepReclaimableMemory().

Security-relevant observations:
- The new path does not touch the coordinator trust boundary, encryption, attestation, authorization, or the SSD prefix-cache at-rest surface (T-041). It does not change TTL, HMAC naming, salt scoping, or purge points.
- It runs inside the existing isLoadingAny-serialized load path. The nativeMiMoReclaimAllowed guard is preserved on the clearCache call. The loop is bounded because poolDropped is set before the single `continue`, so no infinite loop or new DoS surface is evident.
- Dropping the MLX buffer pool and retained free KV segments is a memory-hygiene operation. It may marginally reduce residual data in GPU memory (T-028) and cannot expose data.
- Cancellation is checked before the drop, and the drop is awaited briefly. Availability impact is minimal.

Unverified contract: the implementation of GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments() and busyEnginesKeepReclaimableMemory() is outside the supplied evidence. I could not verify that dropping segments is safe against concurrent engines (e.g. that it does not free memory in use or block indefinitely). The patch comment says engines drop at their next step and the wait is brief. This is an integration question rather than an evidenced regression.

The surrounding base text (reslice, eviction, load flow) is unchanged and was not found to be affected by this change.
